quizzes.title: Global Strategy and Partners: MCQ
quizzes.passage: Tuberculosis has long been one of the world's persistent infectious diseases, and one day each year is set aside to draw attention to it. The observance is meant to raise awareness and to accelerate global efforts to eliminate TB. Much of the global response is guided by the World Health Organization's End TB Strategy, a plan that sets goals for reducing deaths and new cases, with milestones along the way so that progress can be tracked. The strategy applies to all countries, so each nation can measure its results against the same benchmarks. Governments are not working alone, because partner organisations also back national programmes. Their support is meant to sit alongside the work of national health systems. Each year's observance also carries a theme, chosen to keep the message focused on a single idea. The day is marked in India as well, where a number of initiatives have been launched, including a digital platform for monitoring, awareness and citizen participation. The disease calls for attention to prevention, diagnosis and treatment alike, and the response has to address all three. Taken together, the day, the strategy and the partnerships show how the effort against TB is organised across many levels.

questions.q: On which date is World Tuberculosis Day observed every year?
questions.explanation: The booklet states that World TB Day is observed on March 24 every year.

questions.q: Under the WHO End TB Strategy, what is the target for the reduction in TB deaths by 2030?
questions.explanation: The WHO End TB targets for 2030 include a 90% reduction in TB deaths.

questions.q: What is the theme of World Tuberculosis Day 2026?
options: Unite to End TB: Led by Countries, Powered by People
Find TB, Treat TB: Led by Countries, Powered by People
Zero TB Deaths: Led by Countries, Powered by People
Yes! We Can End TB: Led by Countries, Powered by People
questions.explanation: The 2026 theme is 'Yes! We Can End TB: Led by Countries, Powered by People'.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The WHO End TB Strategy has targets set for the year 2030.
Reason (R): The WHO End TB Strategy is a long-term global blueprint.
options: A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but being a long-term blueprint does not explain the 2030 targets.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. WHO End TB Strategy
II. Global Fund and Stop TB Partnership
III. Robert Koch
IV. TB Mukt Urban Ward Initiative
A. Localised intervention in urban TB hotspots
B. Discovery of the TB bacterium in 1882
C. Long-term global blueprint
D. Financial and technical support
questions.explanation: The WHO strategy is a long-term blueprint, Koch discovered the bacterium in 1882, the Global Fund and Stop TB Partnership give financial and technical support, and the urban ward initiative localises intervention.

questions.q:
Read these statements:
I. The Global Fund and Stop TB Partnership strengthen surveillance systems.
II. The WHO End TB Strategy targets an 80% reduction in TB incidence by 2030.
III. The WHO End TB Strategy runs only until 2030.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the strategy's period runs to 2035, so III is wrong.

questions.q:
Read these statements:
I. The Global Fund and Stop TB Partnership promote innovation in diagnostics.
II. World TB Day marks the 1882 discovery of the TB bacterium.
III. The WHO End TB targets for 2030 include a 50% reduction in TB deaths.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while III wrongly gives a 50% death reduction target instead of 90%.

quizzes.title: Global Strategy and Partners: TITA
quizzes.passage: Every year, the world marks one day to focus attention on tuberculosis, a disease that has affected people for generations. The occasion is used to raise awareness and to speed up global efforts. A central reference point for these efforts is the End TB Strategy of the World Health Organization. The strategy is a plan with stated goals, and it applies to every country that chooses to measure its progress against it. Its goals concern the number of deaths from the disease and the number of new cases each year, and it includes milestones that allow progress to be checked. Alongside national governments, several international partner organisations also work on the disease. They support countries in their programmes and help build the capacity needed to carry those programmes out. The observance also carries a theme, which changes from year to year. In India, several initiatives were launched recently, and they have been described as tools for monitoring the disease and encouraging citizens to take part. Taken together, these efforts show how the response to tuberculosis is organised across many levels, from national programmes to global partnerships. Progress depends on governments, health workers and communities working together over a long period.

questions.q: In which year does the WHO End TB Strategy period end? (year)
questions.explanation: The WHO End TB Strategy is a long-term plan that runs to 2035.

questions.q: By which year are the WHO End TB Strategy's targets for TB deaths and incidence set? (year)
questions.explanation: The WHO End TB targets for deaths and incidence are set for 2030.

questions.q: Who discovered the TB bacterium in 1882? (full name)
questions.explanation: World TB Day marks the discovery of the TB bacterium by Robert Koch in 1882.

questions.q: In which year did the WHO End TB Strategy begin? (year)
questions.explanation: The WHO End TB Strategy covers the years 2015 to 2035.

questions.q: What percentage reduction in TB incidence does the WHO End TB Strategy target by 2030? (number, in per cent)
questions.explanation: The WHO End TB targets for 2030 include an 80% reduction in TB incidence.

questions.q: In which year was the TB bacterium discovered? (year)
questions.explanation: The booklet links the discovery of the TB bacterium to 1882.

questions.q: What kind of systems do the Global Fund and Stop TB Partnership strengthen? (one word)
questions.explanation: The booklet says these partners strengthen surveillance systems as one of their focus areas.

quizzes.title: Disease and Drug Resistance: MCQ
quizzes.passage: Tuberculosis is an infectious disease that has affected people for a long time and continues to be a concern for health systems in many countries. The illness can take more than one form, and medical reports describe those forms by the part of the body that is affected. Doctors therefore examine where the infection has settled before deciding how to respond. Treatment depends on medicines, and the choice of medicines depends on the case in hand. Some cases become difficult to manage, and public health officials watch those situations closely. Because of the seriousness of such cases, controlling the disease is treated as a shared task for governments, hospitals and communities rather than a matter for individual patients alone. Diagnosis made in good time matters, and treatment has to be completed as prescribed. Health workers play an important part in identifying cases early, supporting patients through their course of medicine and recording new cases so that the wider picture stays clear. Each stage of this work depends on good records, accurate testing and the steady cooperation of everyone involved in the response to the disease. A day of observance is held each year to raise awareness of the disease, and that day marks the discovery of its bacterial cause in 1882. Several initiatives have been launched in India to support the work, and some of them are monitored through digital platforms that track progress across the country.

questions.q: Which organism causes tuberculosis?
questions.explanation: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.q: Which form of TB affects the lungs and is highly contagious?
questions.explanation: Pulmonary TB affects the lungs and is highly contagious, while extrapulmonary TB is less contagious.

questions.q: Which of these is listed among the first-line drugs used to treat TB?
questions.explanation: Ethambutol is one of the four first-line treatment drugs listed in the booklet.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): MDR-TB is resistant to first-line drugs.
Reason (R): MDR-TB requires second-line drugs, longer treatment and higher cost.
options: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the need for second-line drugs is a consequence of resistance, not its explanation.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Pulmonary TB
II. Extrapulmonary TB
III. MDR-TB
IV. Mycobacterium tuberculosis
A. Bacterium that causes TB
B. Affects organs outside the lungs
C. Resistant to Rifampicin and Isoniazid
D. Affects the lungs and is highly contagious
questions.explanation: Pulmonary TB affects the lungs, extrapulmonary TB affects organs outside them, MDR-TB resists Rifampicin and Isoniazid, and Mycobacterium tuberculosis is the causing bacterium.

questions.q:
Read these statements:
I. TB is an airborne, contagious infectious disease.
II. Extrapulmonary TB is more contagious than pulmonary TB.
III. MDR-TB requires second-line drugs for its treatment.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III are correct, while II reverses the booklet's contagiousness comparison.

questions.q:
Read these statements:
I. TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.
II. Ethambutol is a second-line drug for MDR-TB.
III. TB cannot be cured even with timely diagnosis.
How many of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since Ethambutol is listed as a first-line drug and TB is curable with timely diagnosis.

quizzes.title: Disease and Drug Resistance: TITA
quizzes.passage: Tuberculosis is a long-standing health problem that many countries still struggle with. Its cause is a microscopic germ, and the infection can move from one person to another under the right conditions. Medical reports describe the disease in separate categories, depending on which part of the body it attacks. Patients are usually treated with a set of medicines, and the first medicines used are chosen from a known group. When the infection does not respond to those medicines, the case becomes much harder to manage. Such cases have been described by health authorities as a serious concern for public health. The disease can be prevented and controlled, and timely diagnosis matters a great deal. Health workers play a part in finding cases early, and governments follow the course of the disease closely. Treatment has to be completed as prescribed, and every stage of care depends on accurate testing and steady cooperation among doctors, patients and institutions. A day of observance is held each year to raise awareness, and the response to the disease has been organised through national programmes and a wider global strategy. In India, several initiatives have been launched to monitor the disease and to encourage citizens to take part in its elimination. The campaign is framed around targets that are checked over time, so that the progress made in each period can be seen clearly.

questions.q: Which genus of bacteria causes tuberculosis? (one word)
questions.explanation: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

questions.q: Name the first-line TB drug that is not Ethambutol, Rifampicin or Isoniazid. (one word)
questions.explanation: The first-line treatment drugs listed are Rifampicin, Isoniazid, Pyrazinamide and Ethambutol.

questions.q: Along with Isoniazid, which first-line drug is MDR-TB resistant to? (one word)
questions.explanation: MDR-TB is resistant to Rifampicin and Isoniazid.

questions.q: MDR-TB requires which class of drugs for treatment, in place of standard first-line drugs? (one word)
questions.explanation: MDR-TB requires second-line drugs, longer treatment and higher cost.

questions.q: Which form of TB affects organs outside the lungs? (one word)
questions.explanation: Extrapulmonary TB affects organs outside the lungs and is less contagious.

questions.q: MDR-TB is described as a threat to which global concept? (two words)
questions.explanation: MDR-TB is described as a global health security threat.

questions.q: Through which route does TB spread between people? (one word)
questions.explanation: TB is an airborne, contagious infectious disease.
